memory_verse.label: Bible Portion
memory_verse.text: "When Joseph came to them the next morning, he saw that they were dejected. So he asked Pharaoh's officials who were in custody with him in his master's house, 'Why do you look so sad today?'" - Gen 40:6-7 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The next morning Joseph comes to the two officials and notices something: they look dejected. And rather than being wrapped up in his own troubles, he stops and asks, "Why do you look so sad today?" Think about who is asking this. Joseph himself had every reason to be sad — betrayed by his brothers, enslaved, falsely accused, unjustly imprisoned, and forgotten. Yet here he is, attentive to the sadness of others.

This is a beautiful and challenging picture of compassion. Suffering can turn us inward, making us so consumed by our own pain that we grow blind to the pain around us. But Joseph's own hardship had not hardened him or shut him off. He still had eyes to see when others were hurting, and a heart to reach out and ask.

We can be like Joseph. Even in our own difficult seasons, we can lift our eyes to notice the struggles of those around us. Often, caring for another person in their pain is part of how God carries us through our own. A simple question — "Why do you look so sad today?" — can be the beginning of comfort for someone who feels unseen.

Ask God to keep your heart tender and your eyes open, even in your hard seasons. Look for the dejected faces around you, and be the one who notices and cares. That small kindness can matter more than you know.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Does your own hardship make you blind to others' pain, or more compassionate?
Whose sadness around you have you failed to notice?
How can you be the one who notices and reaches out today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, keep my heart tender even in my hard seasons. Open my eyes to the pain of those around me, and make me the kind of person who notices and reaches out with care. Amen.
